clue.text: A call for help when holding first-rate insulating material

indicators.note: the distress call holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
first-rate means best

explanation.surface: Someone sends a distress call while clutching top-quality lagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos was widely used for fireproof lagging and insulation before its health dangers were known.

clue.text: Cooked lamb left around to munch — in this form perhaps?

definitions.text: Cooked lamb left around to munch — in this form perhaps?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
cooking the lamb here means working its letters into a new order

parts.note: to munch is to eat

explanation.surface: Minced lamb rolled up for eating might well take the shape of the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer itself, hence the question mark: cooked lamb shaped into something to munch.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is minced meat such as lamb shaped into a ball and cooked.

clue.text: California firm's fake American hullabaloo

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
CO is short for company, a firm
phony is the American spelling of phoney, meaning fake

explanation.surface: A Californian company's bogus product causes an uproar in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacophony is a harsh, discordant din, much like a noisy hullabaloo.

clue.text: Part of speech promoted with second half pulled by bishop

indicators.note: the back half of the word is pulled away, leaving its first five letters

parts.note: to promote a product is to advertise it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A grammar term is pushed forward, then cut down by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVERTISED has ten letters, so pulling the second half leaves ADVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is one of the word classes of grammar, modifying verbs and adjectives.

clue.text: Perfectly clean cooking utensil the French kept on board

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the utensil and the article sit within the ship letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship, so goods on board are held within SS
a pot is a cooking utensil
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: A French cook keeps a gleaming pan aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless describes something without a single mark or stain, immaculate.

clue.text: A flat stone turned up in a wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a slab is a flat piece of stone

explanation.surface: A paving stone is dug up in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a wood' suggests a forest, but here it is a kind of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models.

clue.text: Get used — it's a tense time with one Parisienne

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
une is the French feminine for one, as a Parisian woman would say it

explanation.surface: Someone adjusting to life is having a fraught moment with a Parisian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune oneself is to become accustomed or adjusted to something.

clue.text: Ill-natured old leader of Uganda featured in account

indicators.note: the old leader's name appears inside the account letters

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A nasty former Ugandan dictator turns up in a report.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic, said of a person or remark, means sour and sharp-tongued, so bad-tempered.

clue.text: Estate manager stealing diamonds from The Confessor

indicators.note: stealing something from him means taking it away from his name

parts.note: St Edward the Confessor was an English king and saint
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A land agent pinches gems from a saintly king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Confessor is St Edward, so the full name with ST counts; removing a D from STEDWARD gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward runs a large landed property for its owner, collecting rents and overseeing staff.

clue.text: It's able to change form — clasp it tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Something flexible should be gripped firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as an instruction to grip, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as an adjective means mouldable, capable of being shaped.

clue.text: He looks out as former remote-controlled vehicle enters bike races

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the vehicle goes into the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race series
a rover is a remotely driven vehicle, like a Mars rover

explanation.surface: A spectator watches as an old radio-controlled car joins a motorbike race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is outward-looking, focused on other people rather than inner thoughts.

clue.text: Measure depth of safe inlet of the sea

definitions.meaning: to ... water is to measure how deep it is
a narrow sea channel or inlet

explanation.surface: A sailor checks the depth of a sheltered bay.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers taking soundings, being solid and secure, and a strait such as Plymouth Sound.

clue.text: Every one sat in a desk? That's how pupils need to be

definitions.text: That's how pupils need to be

indicators.note: each one is seated inside the desk word

parts.note: a desk is a kind of table
each means every one

explanation.surface: Every child sits at a desk, ready to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachable means able and willing to learn, which a pupil should be.

clue.text: Freelance soldier infiltrating summer camp

indicators.note: the soldier sneaks into the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A hired gun sneaks into a holiday camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is informal for a mercenary, a soldier hired by whoever pays.

clue.text: Leader abandons genuine regret

indicators.note: the first letter leaves the word

parts.note: true means genuine

explanation.surface: A boss walks out, feeling real remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue as a noun is sorrow or remorse for something done.

clue.text: Caught by public area of land I'll go in to stir

indicators.note: the inner letters are captured within the public land word

parts.note: a common is open land for public use

indicators.note: I will go inside the word to

parts.note: I'll is I will, so the letter I is the one that goes in

explanation.surface: A cricketer is caught near the village green, which stirs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll go in to' reads literally: I goes into TO, making TIO, which COMMON then catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a fuss or disturbance, which is what a commotion is.

clue.text: Mum's best lesson, diligence is wasted

indicators.note: wasted letters are wrecked and remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A mother's wisdom that hard work is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it is the word meaning silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says keeping quiet is the wisest course, so being mum is best.

clue.text: A Nigerian island's bad smell

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: An island in Nigeria has an unpleasant whiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibo (Igbo) are one of the largest ethnic groups of south-east Nigeria.

clue.text: Women's emblem includes this band

indicators.note: the phrase includes the answer within its letters, across the word break

explanation.surface: A women's group's badge features a band's logo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group of musicians performing together.

clue.text: With boring MO and doctor I dropped in ahead of time

indicators.note: the letter I is dropped inside the word for ahead of time

parts.note: early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: A medical officer and a doctor arrive early with a dull routine.
explanation.walkthrough: MO looks like a medical officer to go with the doctor; here it is modus operandi, a way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearily means in a dull, tedious manner, so doing something with a boring method.

clue.text: E.g. almond, almost entire, prepared as sustenance

parts.note: an almond is an example of a nut

indicators.note: the shortened letters are prepared, made up into a new order
almost means the last letter is left off

explanation.surface: An almond, nearly whole, is made ready as food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ENTIRE to ENTIR, and 'prepared' rearranges that to RIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that nourishes, providing sustenance.

clue.text: Where across clues are creating arguments

definitions.meaning: across answers are written in the grid's horizontal lines

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is self-referential: across entries sit in horizontal lines of the grid, rhyming with 'cows'. The second sense rhymes with 'cows' too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both horizontal lines of squares and noisy disputes.

clue.text: It's a scam nicking book from top of shelf

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a shelf rests on top of a bracket, a wall support

explanation.surface: A con involving swiping a volume off the top shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of shelf' looks like a first-letter pick, but it is the bracket that a shelf sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme for making money, a swindle.

clue.text: Chief god clasps ring fashioned from Yggdrasil perhaps

indicators.note: the god's name clasps the ring inside it

parts.note: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon name for Odin, chief of the Norse gods
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Odin holds a ring carved from the world tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Yggdrasil is the giant ash tree of Norse myth, so anything made from it would be timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made from a tree's timber is wooden, Yggdrasil being an example of a tree.

clue.text: Most like squalor, smut and slime when working

indicators.note: working means the letters are put into action, rearranged

explanation.surface: The filthiest places are full of grime and slime when in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Slummiest is the superlative of slummy, so most resembling a squalid slum.

clue.text: Higher urban area now put in disarray

indicators.note: letters in disarray are jumbled, so they can be reordered

explanation.surface: A smart district of a city has now been left in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptown is the residential district of a US city away from the centre, often on higher ground.

clue.text: Some memoir on Yeltsin as a form of satire

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A book about the Russian president as a send-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony, saying the opposite of what is meant, is a common tool of satirical writing.

clue.text: Prof's post has nothing for a group of singers

indicators.note: the post has one letter in place of another
nothing goes in for the letter a

parts.note: a professor holds a chair at a university
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A professor's job offers nothing for a choral group.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church.

clue.text: Came across a sailor initially stranded on island — Bones

parts.note: met means came across
a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A castaway sailor is found marooned on an island, reduced to bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' looks like a nickname for a ship's doctor, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsi are the five long bones of the foot between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Endless energy seen by seabird on the wing without end

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: ala is the anatomical term for a wing

explanation.surface: A seabird flying tirelessly with boundless energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without any end.

clue.text: Cardigan possibly to court little Eleanor on return

parts.note: to woo is to court

indicators.note: on return means read backwards

parts.note: Nell is a pet form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: A suitor woos Nell, who comes back to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardigan' could be the Welsh town or the earl; here it is the knitted jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is an example of a knitted garment, which can be called a woollen.
